content_voiceover: This slide shows the survival outcomes and toxicity profile from the ELIANA trial at two years of follow up. The overall survival curve shows a survival probability of seventy six percent at twelve months and sixty six percent at twenty four months among all seventy nine infused patients, with twenty five events recorded. Notably, the median overall survival was not reached, or NE, at two years, which is a remarkable result for a relapsed refractory pediatric ALL population that historically had very poor prognosis. On the right, the table outlines grade three and four adverse reactions. Cytokine release syndrome, the hallmark toxicity of CAR T cell therapy, occurred at grade three or four severity in forty eight percent of patients. Hematologic laboratory abnormalities were extremely common, with decreased white blood cell count in ninety seven percent, decreased lymphocyte count in ninety six percent, decreased neutrophil count in ninety five percent, decreased platelets in seventy seven percent, and decreased hemoglobin in forty eight percent. These cytopenias reflect both the lymphodepleting chemotherapy given before infusion and the CAR T cell expansion process itself, and underscore why careful monitoring and supportive care are essential after CAR T cell therapy.
keypoints: Median OS not reached at two years follow up in ELIANA trial
OS rate seventy six percent at twelve months, sixty six percent at twenty four months
Grade three four CRS occurred in forty eight percent of patients
Severe cytopenias nearly universal, WBC decrease ninety seven percent, neutrophil decrease ninety five percent
keypoint_voiceover: Remember that ELIANA showed median overall survival not reached at two years, with a sixty six percent survival rate at twenty four months. The major toxicity to know for boards is cytokine release syndrome, occurring at grade three or four severity in almost half of patients, alongside near universal cytopenias.
